shots.name: Design intent
shots.meaning: Define silhouette, volume, proportion and material behaviour before engineering.
shots.subject: A length of charcoal-blue wool crepe
shots.action: A designer tests its fall over one open hand.
shots.environment: Bright white fabric-evaluation counter; close oblique angle.
avoid: Garment or toile implied by unsewn cloth
shots.prompt: A single candid documentary photograph commissioned for a high-end fashion design and technical product development studio, not an illustration. Shot on a full-frame camera with a 50mm lens, believable working moment, no glossy CGI or oversharpened fabric. One scene, one action. Framing has a central subject that survives responsive cropping. No collage, graphic overlays, drawn dotted lines, digital effects, diagrams on clothing, fake basting, decorative staging, busy background, text, logos or brand names. No beige color cast. Any person is an adult professional; hands have normal proportions, five fingers, natural positions, no jewelry. Garments and objects obey physical gravity. Landscape 4:3. Close side-angle photograph of one adult textile designer's open left hand, palm down, emerging from a plain white shirt cuff at the left edge, supporting one continuous length of deep charcoal-blue wool crepe over the back of the hand so the fabric falls vertically in two or three soft gravity-driven folds toward a clean white counter. The designer is evaluating weight and drape. Cloth is unsewn yardage with one simple selvedge; it must never look like a shirt or a skirt. Focus on the falling cloth and natural hand. No other props, no face, no mannequin, no room decor. Airy clean white background. Do not arrange a decorative fabric sculpture.
